## Motivating example

What do you think will be the output of this code?

```{r, eval=F, echo=T}
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
y <- c(0, 1)

x + y
```

## Motivating example

```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
y <- c(0, 1)

x + y
```

What has happened here?

## Vector recycling

**Vector recycling:** Repeating elements of the shorter vector to match the length of the longer vector

```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
y <- c(0, 1)

x + y
```

## Vector recycling

```{r, warning=T}
x <- c(1, 2, 3)
y <- c(0, 1)

x + y
```

If the length of the longer vector is not a multiple of the length of the shorter vector, R will give a warning -- but will still produce output!

## Huber loss

```{r}
huber_loss <- function(y, y_hat, gamma){
  res <- y - y_hat
  ifelse(abs(res) < gamma, 
         0.5*res^2, 
         gamma*abs(res) - 0.5*gamma^2)
}

huber_loss(y = c(2, 2, 3, 4), y_hat = c(1.5, 2.5), gamma = 1)
```

* How would I modify my function to ensure `y` and `y_hat` have the same length?
* The current code runs fine, even if the output is not what we want. How would I catch this bug in my code?

## Error handling

```{r, error = T}
huber_loss <- function(y, y_hat, gamma){
  if(length(y) != length(y_hat)){
    stop("y and y_hat must have the same length")
  }
  
  res <- y - y_hat
  ifelse(abs(res) < gamma, 
         0.5*res^2, 
         gamma*abs(res) - 0.5*gamma^2)
}

huber_loss(y = c(2, 2, 3, 4), y_hat = c(1.5, 2.5), gamma = 1)
```

## Finding bugs: unit testing!

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
library(testthat)
```

```{r}
test_that("Huber loss length error", {
  expect_error(huber_loss(y = c(2, 2, 3, 4), 
                          y_hat = c(1.5, 2.5), gamma = 1))
})
```

## Finding bugs: unit testing!

Let's also check that we get an error when `y` is the shorter vector:

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
library(testthat)
```

```{r}
test_that("Huber loss length error", {
  expect_error(huber_loss(y = c(2, 2, 3, 4), 
                          y_hat = c(1.5, 2.5), gamma = 1))
  expect_error(huber_loss(y = c(1, 2),
                          y_hat = c(1, 2, 3), gamma = 1))
})
```

## Finding bugs: unit testing!

We can also test that our function produces the desired values:

$$\rho_\gamma(Y_i, \widehat{Y}_i) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}(Y_i - \widehat{Y}_i)^2 & |Y_i - \widehat{Y}_i| < \gamma \\ \gamma|Y_i - \widehat{Y}_i| - \frac{1}{2}\gamma^2 & |Y_i - \widehat{Y}_i| \geq \gamma \end{cases}$$

```{r}
test_that("Huber loss value test 1", {
  expect_equal(huber_loss(y = 1, y_hat = 0.5, gamma = 1),
               0.125)
})
```

## Finding bugs: unit testing!

This implementation has a bug, but our test passes:

```{r}
huber_loss <- function(y, y_hat, gamma){
  if(length(y) != length(y_hat)){
    stop("y and y_hat must have the same length")
  }
  
  res <- y - y_hat
  ifelse(res < gamma, 
         0.5*res^2, 
         gamma*abs(res) - 0.5*gamma^2)
}
```

```{r}
test_that("Huber loss value test 1", {
  expect_equal(huber_loss(y = 1, y_hat = 0.5, gamma = 1),
               0.125)
})
```

## Finding bugs: unit testing!

```{r}
huber_loss <- function(y, y_hat, gamma){

  }
```

```{r, error = T}
test_that("Huber loss value test 1", {
```
